extracted.intended_audience: mathematics department faculty, assessment coordinators, and undergraduate curriculum developers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and examples for designing and operating a comprehensive departmental assessment program for undergraduate mathematics, including data collection, test design, placement, technology evaluation, and research-informed pedagogical assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student portfolios with common questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use portfolios to measure conceptual growth over time: five common questions (aligned with five educational threads) that all students must respond to in each core mathematics course. Each response is a paragraph up to a half-page typewritten and included in the portfolio for each of the four courses. Subsequent portfolios must contain responses from previous courses to show individual growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes example prompts (e.g., 'Define a function. Give an example of a function from this course and explain its use.'; 'Discuss how a math modeling process is used in this course. Describe the impact of “assumptions” and how one can “validate” their model.'). Intended for self-evaluation and longitudinal tracking of student conceptual development.

rubrics_metrics.name: West Point Goal 1: mathematics as communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn to use mathematics as a medium of communication that integrates numeric, graphic, and symbolic representations, structures ideas, and facilitates synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: West Point Goal 2: deductive character of mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the deductive character of mathematics, where a few principles are internalized and most notions are deduced therewith.

rubrics_metrics.name: West Point Goal 3: curiosity and experimental disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn that curiosity and an experimental disposition are essential, and that universal truths are established through proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: West Point Goal 4: individual responsibility for learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand that learning mathematics is an individual responsibility, and that texts and instructors facilitate the process, but that concepts are stable and skills are transient and pertain only to particular applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: West Point Goal 5: mathematics is useful
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn that mathematics is useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: West Point Goal 6: aggressive problem solving
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage aggressive problem solving skills by providing ample opportunities throughout the core curriculum to solve meaningful practical problems requiring the integration of fundamental ideas encompassing one or more blocks of lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: West Point Goal 7: develop mathematical thought processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop the ability to think mathematically through the introduction of the fundamental thought processes of discrete, continuous, and probabilistic mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: West Point Goal 8: scholarly habits and lifelong learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop good scholarly habits promoting student independence and life-long learning ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: West Point Goal 9: transition from high school to college
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an orderly transition from the environment of the high school curriculum to the environment of an upper divisional college classroom.

rubrics_metrics.name: West Point Goal 10: integrate computer technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate computer technology throughout the four-semester curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: West Point Goal 11: integrate mathematical modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate mathematical modeling throughout the curriculum to access the rich application problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-school/background data collection for predictive analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect high school data for entering freshmen from admissions: SAT verbal and math scores, high school GPAs, high school attended, and initial choice of major.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these variables to examine longitudinal outcomes and as inputs to predictive formulas (e.g., math readiness scores) for placement and program evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of CIRP background survey data
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquire Cooperative Institutional Research Program (CIRP) background survey data during freshmen summer orientation for institution-specific and national comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify CIRP variables associated with student success and merge with departmental data for research and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course administrative data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect course data including overall and sectional enrollment, student IDs by section, instructors of each section, times and locations of courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize data by semester with student anonymity coding to support sectional analyses and comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Achievement data via common finals with three cognitive types
rubrics_metrics.description: Administer common final examinations (multiple choice) for core courses including three cognitive question types: skills, concepts, and applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use common finals to determine extent of mastery, enable comparisons among sections and instructional modalities, and to inform construction/refinement of future test questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of common finals by faculty committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty committees construct common finals using questions submitted by instructors; tests are evaluated for appropriateness of content, question format and style, and item difficulty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty involvement and iterative refinement increases representativeness and clarity of exams and fosters departmental dialogue about assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-test analyses: reliability, validity, item analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform post-test analyses including test reliability coefficients, item analyses, overall and sectional means and standard deviations, and score distributions for each administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment coordinator compiles item-level data and provides faculty with printouts and electronic data to aid interpretation and future test construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Likert-scale departmental surveys for affective variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Administer in-house departmental surveys using Likert rating scales to gauge student opinions, learning skills and styles, motivation, and mathematical ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merge affective survey variables with quantitative achievement data to analyze predictors of success and inform course modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data storage, privacy, and analysis infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Store data in electronic files on departmental server with limited access due to student privacy concerns; use SPSS-Windows for statistical analyses and create/merge datasets as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain data security while enabling creation of specific datasets combining academic, student, grade, and survey files for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods for program evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use statistical techniques (mean comparisons, t-tests, Pearson correlations, regression analysis, longitudinal studies) to compare groups and evaluate downstream outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include comparing traditional vs technology-based instruction, ESP vs traditional calculus, and validating placement formulas over semesters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math Readiness Scores for placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate Math Readiness Scores for entering freshmen using a multiple regression formula based on high school math GPA, College Board math scores, and whether the student had taken calculus in high school. Determine decision thresholds for placement into engineering calculus vs pre-calculus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate and modify the formula each semester using course grades to maximize predictive capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emerging Scholars Program (ESP) augmented calculus evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate ESP calculus (augmented engineering calculus) using required problem-solving sessions supervised by faculty and undergrad tutors; compare outcomes (course grades, common final scores, grade distributions) with traditional sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statistical significance testing to justify program adoption/expansion; incorporate faculty, tutor and student feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developmental course pilots and non-cognitive predictors
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot computer-assisted, self-paced versions of developmental courses (e.g., college algebra), and use regression analyses combining survey-derived non-cognitive items (beliefs about math ability, organization, learning style) with grades to identify predictors of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use findings to select and refine instructional modalities and support options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology integration assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess technology use by measuring: student pacing benefits, downstream performance in advanced courses, network/software reliability issues, and congruity between lecture and computer assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both quantitative outcomes and qualitative feedback to modify technology use each semester (e.g., expansion of a Mathematics Emporium).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring sectional outcome congruence (grades vs common finals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare sectional mean common final scores with assigned course grades (compute correlations) to identify incongruence between grading practices and measured student learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide anonymous sectional data to instructors to enable self-analysis and collaborative improvement of teaching and grading practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of focus groups for program evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include focus groups to obtain students' qualitative views about course format, philosophy, expectations, and sense of community for programs like ESP calculus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine uniformly positive/negative themes from focus groups with quantitative data to evaluate and refine programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment as consensus-building and accountability tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Use departmental assessment to involve faculty, build consensus around core content and measurable objectives, inform curricular decisions, demonstrate stewardship of resources, and provide evidence to external constituencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment outcomes should serve multiple stakeholders (students, faculty, administration, state agencies) and support program planning and ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACE teaching cycle (Activities/Discussion/Exercises)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement a weekly ACE cycle: (A) computer lab activities designed to foster mental constructions, (C) classroom discussion to reflect and convert constructions to mental concepts, and (E) exercises to reinforce and extend knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ACE as the pedagogical structure whose implementation can be monitored and used as an indirect indicator that desired mental constructions have been fostered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual assessment questions: mental constructions and mathematical learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Design assessment to ask two kinds of questions: (1) Has the student made the mental constructions (actions, processes, objects, schemas) called for by research? (2) Has the student learned the mathematics in the course?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because direct measurement of mental constructions is impractical in courses, use indirect measures (participation, completion of computer tasks, group cooperation, written work) plus tests of procedural/application competence to infer constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-informed inference about learning from participation and performance
rubrics_metrics.description: If pedagogy operated as intended (student participated in activities, cooperated in group, completed assignments, performed reasonably on exams), then infer that students likely made the targeted mental constructions and learned underlying mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep records of written work, classroom participation, and group meetings to support these inferences; combine with testing evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment focus on depth and difficulty over breadth
rubrics_metrics.description: When constructing examinations, prioritize asking the hardest possible questions about the material believed to be learned rather than trying to cover as much material as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments should evaluate how hard tests were and how much material they covered as part of judging course success; this aligns with viewing courses as increasing students' knowledge rather than just covering topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of qualitative research methods to inform assessment design
rubrics_metrics.description: Use interviews, teaching experiments, and other qualitative research methods to develop operational understandings of mental constructions and map these to curriculum topics, recognizing these methods are labor-intensive and impractical for routine course assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use findings from such research to design indirect, practical assessment components for courses (e.g., ACE activities, targeted test items).
